name: New Brunswick Drug Plan (Plan D)
who: NB residents with valid Medicare card and no private/other government drug coverage; also those with private plan whose drug is not on its formulary for the condition, or who hit its annual/lifetime max. Dependants 18 and under pay no premium but a parent must enrol. Payor of last resort.
age: All ages (parent enrols for dependants 18 and under)
route: Application form + other-coverage supporting form (if applicable) + direct-deposit/pre-authorized payment form; gnb.ca/drugplan; inquiries 1-800-332-3692 (Mon-Fri 8-5)
reason: Not in built list (NB Prescription Drug Program is the separate Plan U-style program). Fetched premiums page and eligibility-plan-d.pdf (https://www.gnb.ca/content/dam/GNB3/t/hw-sme/nb-drug-plans/policy-manual/eligibility-plan-d.pdf). Eligibility page https://www.gnb.ca/en/topic/health-wellness/nb-drug-plans/enrol-drug-plan.html also fetched. Broadly relevant to low-income/uninsured people incl. disability.

name: Health Services Hearing Aid Program
who: Department of Social Development clients and their dependents with an NBCase health card showing Supplementary/HA eligibility (or yellow card OTH=Y / SUPP=X); no other medical coverage for full benefits.
what: Pays for basic hearing aids (max $1,000 per aid, 1 per ear every 5 years), repairs and ear molds; prior approval required.
age: All ages (children via Special Needs Children program)
route: Prior approval from Health Services Program with audiologist report, audiogram, estimate; NB licensed hearing aid provider; 506-453-2001
reason: Policy PDF dated 2026 fetched and read via pdftotext. Listed on old SD persons-with-disabilities hub (www2) but NOT on the new gnb.ca topic page; the HTML program page was a JS shell. Same Health Services family as built equipment programs, so could be folded into that record.

name: Health Services Vision Program (adults)
who: Social Development clients and dependents aged 19+ (or special health needs under Family Income Security Act) with white health card optical coverage or yellow card Y/X under OPT; no other vision coverage.
what: Free eye exams (every 2 yrs; yearly if diabetic), selected frames, corrective lenses, cases.
age: 19+ (18 and under covered by Healthy Smiles Clear Vision)
route: Via optometrist/optician with valid Health Services card
reason: Distinct from built Healthy Smiles Clear Vision (children) and Ocular prosthesis. Tied to social assistance health card, so may fold into Social Assistance record; user's call.

name: Public Housing (Housing NB)
who: Low-income households under income ceilings (1-bedroom $45,000 urban/$50,500 rural; 2-bed $57,500/$59,500; 3-bed $63,000/$67,500) who are in crowded/inadequate housing or pay 30%+ of income on rent.
what: Rent-geared-to-income units owned by Housing NB (about 30% of income per related FAQ).
route: Call Housing NB 1-833-733-7835 or local Social Development office; waitlist
reason: Page does not mention disability; general low-income housing. Rent supplement programs are built but public housing units are a separate program.

name: New Brunswick Seniors' Home Renovation Tax Credit
who: NB residents 65+ or family members living with a senior; not income-tested.
what: Refundable credit of 10% of up to $10,000 accessibility/safety renovations (ramps, grab bars, walk-in tubs): max $1,000/yr.
route: Claim on NB personal income tax return (NB428 area); info 1-800-669-7070
reason: Page does not state tax years or an end date; confirm still in force. Seniors accessibility, not disability-specific.

name: Childcare Assistance Program (with referral for children with developmental needs)
who: Parents of children 0-5 in non-designated facilities or 5-12 in school-age programs, household income up to $80,000 sliding scale; parents working/studying or with parent or child-program referral (e.g. Early Intervention, VIVA, APSEA, medical).
what: Sliding-scale subsidy toward childcare fees, paid to provider.
route: Apply through Social Development / program line 1-833-221-9339
reason: General low-income program; disability link only through referral pathways. Name on gnb.ca is Childcare Assistance Program (formerly Day Care Assistance Program). Dollar scale not published on page.

name: Early Intervention Program (Family and Early Childhood agencies)
who: Families of children 8 and under with developmental delay or identified at risk by screening/Public Health.
what: Free in-home visits, family support, developmental childcare (age 3-5, up to 12 hrs/week tuition) via 7 agencies.
route: Contact local Family and Early Childhood agency
reason: Details come from WebSearch snippet of guidelines PDF https://www2.gnb.ca/content/dam/gnb/Departments/ed/pdf/ELCC/ECHDPE/EarlyIntervention.pdf which I did NOT fetch, so unverified; fetch before building. Preschool Autism Program is already built.

name: Medicare Out-of-Province Hostel Facilities and Meal Allowance
who: Outpatients whose physician requires care outside NB (within Canada) needing 3+ consecutive hostel nights, service unavailable in NB; prior approval mandatory.
what: Hostel including meals up to $150/day; escort meals up to $75.57/day; apartment up to $4,000/month for stays over 30 days. Travel not covered.
route: Prior approval request by physician, social worker or care coordinator to Medicare (fax 506-457-7671)
reason: Only medical-travel help found; not disability-specific, so borderline. Lower priority.
